themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — USDJPY 155-158.5 range, intervention credibility test ongoing, BOJ hike Oct/Dec
themes.summary: The G2 coordinated intervention regime remains fully active but is entering a credibility test phase. Recap: Japan MoF deployed record ¥11.73T in solo intervention across Apr-May 2026 that ultimately failed, with USDJPY hitting a 40-year low near 163-164. On Jul 30 Japan intervened in NY hours. The US Treasury confirmed direct participation on Jul 31 — Fed NY sold euros for yen via Goldman and Morgan Stanley — the first joint US-Japan intervention in nearly 30 years. USDJPY printed its post-intervention low of 155.20-155.25 on Aug 3. Both Bessent and Trump publicly endorsed further action. Japan MoF confirmed use of the FIMA repo facility for future interventions, removing the US Treasury-selling tail risk. BOJ voted 8-1 to hold at 1%; with only Takata dissenting for a hike, September is likely off the table — October or December more probable for the next BOJ move. UBS and OCBC flagged that without complementary BOJ tightening, intervention buys time but not a structural reversal. The week of Aug 4-8 was telling: USDJPY recovered from the 155.20 low back to the mid-158s as JPY broadly underperformed on the ABSENCE of follow-up intervention, underscoring that the yen's fundamental drivers — wide rate differentials, negative real rates, weak household spending (-3.3% in June vs +1% expected) — remain intact. On Aug 7, the July NFP printed -23K vs +80K consensus with -103K prior revisions, sending USDJPY back down to 157.65. Post-NFP EUR/USD is above 1.15 and GBP/USD is approaching 1.3500 — broad USD weakness is now adding a fundamental tailwind to the intervention regime. The critical dynamic for the week of Aug 10-15: if USDJPY drifts back above 158 without official response, carry traders will test MoF resolve again. Bessent reiterated Washington's support for Japan on Aug 7. The range 155-158.5 is the active intervention corridor; breaks in either direction are high-impact events.

implications.JPY: MAXIMUM tailwind from dual-authority intervention with FIMA repo mechanism and explicit Bessent re-entry warning, PLUS catastrophic NFP that structurally weakens the opposing rate-differential argument. But JPY underperformed week of Aug 4-8 when no follow-up intervention materialised — the market is testing MoF resolve. All JPY-cross SHORT positions face active G2 headwind. BOJ hike Oct/Dec provides a secondary fundamental pillar. Japan weak household spending (-3.3% in June) complicates BOJ's urgency to hike.
implications.USD: ACUTE BEARISH from the Aug 7 NFP shock — -23K vs +80K consensus with -103K prior revisions has collapsed Sep hike probability and removed the USD carry narrative near-term. Broad USD under pressure: EUR/USD above 1.15, GBP/USD near 1.35, DXY at key support. USDJPY at 157.65 and gravitating toward intervention corridor floor.
implications.EUR: EUR/JPY sold by the mechanism of Fed NY intervention (euros-for-yen). EUR/USD paradoxically firming above 1.15 as USD weakness post-NFP dominates. Testing major resistance under highly unusual circumstances per ING — this is a USD story, not an EUR story. Watch 1.1560 as near-term high.
implications.GBP: GBP/JPY under dual pressure from intervention and USD-positive-carry unwind. GBP/USD rallying toward 1.3500 on USD weakness but BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance.
implications.CHF: CHF/JPY lower. CHF gains mild safe-haven bid in risk-off post-NFP. USDCHF under pressure from broad USD weakness.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower; CAD dynamics primarily driven by Section 338 tariff theme. USD weakness post-NFP partially offsets USDCAD upside but Aug 19 tariff binary dominates.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY lower. AUD/USD modestly supported by broad USD weakness from NFP but risk-off tone from labour shock is a countervailing drag. Watch for AUDJPY 93-94 as intervention-corridor support.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDJPY under pressure.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY below 155.20 (post-intervention low) = corporate hedger stop-loss loops activate, intervention 'winning' decisively. USDJPY above 158.5 (pre-NFP consolidation high) = carry trade reasserting, MoF resolve tested — watch for verbal intervention first. USDJPY back above 160 = market overpowering coordinated defence, theme credibility breaks. Any official MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further action = theme ends immediately. BOJ hike at Oct or Dec meeting = fundamental support materialises, reduces intervention burden. Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (Warsh speech) is next major binary for USD direction and hence USDJPY.

themes.title: Warsh Fed under NFP shock — Sep hike odds collapsing, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (18 days) is the live USD binary
themes.summary: The Warsh hawkish regime is structurally intact but has been materially challenged by the Aug 7 NFP disaster. The Jul 29 FOMC held at 3.5-3.75% with three hawkish dissents advocating a 25bp hike; the 30-yr yield surged to 5.21% (19-year high) and Warsh confirmed forward guidance elimination is permanent. Median 2026 dot raised to 3.8%, with 9 of 18 members projecting at least one hike. Per CME FedWatch, Sep hike odds were 61.9% as of Aug 4 — pre-NFP. The Aug 7 print of -23K vs +80K consensus (unemployment 4.1%, prior months revised -103K combined) is the most consequential US labour miss in the current cycle and has directly pressured Warsh's hawkish stance. Sep hike odds have collapsed post-print. The market reaction post-NFP confirms the scale of the repricing: EUR/USD surging above 1.15 to a fresh multi-week high near 1.1560; GBP/USD approaching 1.3500; DXY near 100.00 and testing key support. No August FOMC meeting means three weeks of positioning into Jackson Hole with no policy anchor. Warsh described his Jackson Hole keynote as 'a blank piece of paper' at the Jul 29 press conference, explicitly declining to pre-commit the speech direction — an unusually high uncertainty premium for a Fed chair speech. He noted he would consult with his 15-member external expert panel before Jackson Hole and 'may or may not' share what is 'ready for prime time.' Post-NFP that speech is now the single most important near-term USD catalyst: hawkish signal (hike still on table) = USD recovers 150-200 pips across board; dovish pivot or soft language = USD carry narrative collapses and current weakness extends. Warsh has also indicated he expects to frame 'larger policy questions' at Jackson Hole rather than near-term rate path — but post-NFP markets will force him to address the labour data. The Fed is additionally considering reducing meeting frequency, which would amplify each remaining 2026 event's market impact. Political complexity persists: Trump publicly framed the FOMC as obstructionist, a narrative that intensifies if labour data continues to deteriorate.

implications.USD: NEAR-TERM BEARISH shock confirmed — EUR/USD above 1.15, GBP near 1.35, DXY near 100 as of Aug 7-8. Structural hawkish carry bid now requires Jackson Hole reaffirmation to re-engage. The three-week void of policy guidance into Jackson Hole means headline USD pairs will be extremely reactive to any Warsh commentary or data releases (CPI, PPI, retail sales pre-Aug 27).
implications.JPY: Rate differential headwind from Warsh narrative is now significantly reduced by NFP miss — do not fade JPY strength solely on carry differential. USDJPY bearish case has dual drivers: intervention AND fading hike probability post-NFP.
implications.EUR: EUR/USD headwind from ECB-vs-Fed differential sharply narrowing post-NFP. EUR/USD surging toward 1.1560 multi-week high. Any Warsh dovish pivot at Jackson Hole = significant EUR/USD upside toward 1.17-1.18 range.
implications.GBP: GBP/USD rallying toward 1.3500 on broad USD weakness. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR but GBP benefits from USD-weakness theme. Watch 1.3500 as key resistance.
implications.CAD: Mixed — USD structural bid from Warsh narrative was offsetting CAD tariff weakness; with NFP miss that USD tailwind erodes further. USDCAD may consolidate pre-Aug 19. Aug 19 tariff hard binary remains the dominant CAD driver.
implications.AUD: Modest headwind from Warsh carry narrative further reduced with NFP. RBA on hold with easing bias; AUD/USD rallying on broad USD weakness but AUD lags in risk-off. Watch AUDUSD for continuation above 0.6600.
implications.NZD: RBNZ same as AUD. NZDUSD benefits from USD weakness.
implications.CHF: SNB in easing mode; USDCHF under pressure from NFP-driven USD weakness. CHF may outperform on safe-haven demand post-labour shock.

themes.watchLevel: Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 — Warsh keynote (Friday Aug 28) is the primary binary: hawkish signal restores USD carry bid; dovish signal extends current weakness. Pre-JH data to watch: US CPI (Aug 12-13 est.), PPI, retail sales — any upside CPI surprise partially restores USD. Sep FOMC (Sep 16) is the hard policy event. Any Warsh speech or interview in the 18-day interim that provides hike guidance = major mover. Sub-3.0% CPI print = dovish tolerance returns, theme ends. DXY closing and sustaining below 99.50 = market rejecting hawkish read entirely. 30-yr yield sustained above 5.5% = fiscal concerns overtaking carry narrative.

themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs effective Aug 19 — 50% on ~$20B of goods, USMCA no shield, 10 days to binary
themes.summary: The Section 338 binary is now 10 days from resolution with no deal in sight and retaliation threats mounting. Three presidential proclamations signed Jul 20 invoke Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 — its first modern use since the 1940s — imposing 50% duties on approximately $20B of Canadian goods (autos, dairy, alcohol, plus wine, cement, furniture, hockey sticks, clothing, seeds and more per annex) effective August 19, 2026 at 12:01am ET. The duty stacks on top of all existing tariffs and USMCA certification provides zero relief — a structural break from every prior Canada tariff action where USMCA compliance guaranteed exemption. The administration chose Section 338 specifically because it has no procedural requirements: unlike Section 301 (requires USTR investigation) or Section 232 (requires national security determination), Section 338 allows presidential proclamation alone. Each of the three proclamations cites a distinct Canadian discriminatory practice: provincial alcohol board bans on US liquor (Canadian imports of US alcoholic beverages dropped ~81% from $718M to $137M); dairy quota rules disadvantaging US suppliers; and Canada's surtax on US-made autos (Canadian motor vehicle exports to the US fell ~22% over the year ending March 2026). Section 338 tariffs carry no statutory time limit — unlike IEEPA and Section 122 — meaning they are permanent unless explicitly revoked. CBP is still finalising HTSUS modifications and implementation guidance, meaning the full scope of covered goods has not finished settling. PM Carney has vowed WTO-consistent retaliatory measures in response, following the pattern of all prior tariff escalations. No formal Canada retaliation proclamation has been published as of Aug 9 but preparation is evidently underway. The USMCA mandatory six-year review commenced July 1, 2026 — three weeks before the Section 338 proclamations — and the agreement is not automatically renewed; if parties fail to agree, it moves to annual reviews with possible termination in 2036. The NFP-driven USD weakness creates a near-term counterweight to USDCAD upside, compressing the pre-Aug 19 range, but the Aug 19 binary outcome dwarfs any near-term USD oscillation in significance.

implications.CAD: STRONG structural headwind — 50% stacking duties on ~$20B of exports, permanent statutory authority, no USMCA exemption. Vol elevated both directions into Aug 19. USDCAD technically constructive above 1.40 but NFP-driven USD weakness has capped near-term upside and compressed the range. Widen stops, reduce size on all CAD crosses. Canadian importers facing 50% duty cliff on Aug 19 have already pulled forward shipments, creating distorted near-term trade data.
implications.USD: Moderate tariff-narrative tailwind from USDCAD, but Aug 7 NFP shock creates significant countervailing USD weakness. Net: USDCAD may consolidate 1.39-1.42 range ahead of Aug 19 binary rather than trend.
implications.MXN: Elevated secondary exposure — USDMXN moves can telegraph CAD next-session. Mexico separately facing Section 301 successor regime at 10-12.5%.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EU separately under 15% tariff ceiling from Jul 1; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses in a CAD-shock scenario.
implications.AUD: Indirect risk-off if CAD volatility spills into broader commodity bloc on Aug 19; AUDCAD may be volatile around the binary.

themes.watchLevel: Aug 19 12:01am ET is the primary hard binary — 10 days away. Pre-Aug 19 Canada capitulation or bilateral deal = sharp CAD relief 100-150 pips, retire theme. Tariffs land as scheduled = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, extend CAD-bearish bias. Canada retaliation proclamation published pre- or post-Aug 19 = CAD vol surge 100+ pips both directions. Any Section 338 legal challenge or court injunction pausing collection = uncertainty spike. Any USMCA emergency session called specifically to address Section 338 = modest CAD relief. CBP finalising HTSUS scope modifications may narrow or widen covered goods before Aug 19. Watch USDMXN as a leading indicator. Section 338's permanent nature (no statutory sunset) means theme does not auto-expire on Aug 19 even if tariffs land — it persists until explicitly revoked or superseded.
